yutNori.title: Yut Nori
yutNori.subtitle: Play Korea's traditional board game online — against 1–3 AI players or with 2–4 people on one device. Backdo, stacking, capturing and shortcuts included.

guide.title: Yut Nori rules and how to play

howToPlay.title: How to play
items: Take turns throwing four sticks and move a piece by the result. Pieces start outside the start/finish corner (bottom right) and travel counterclockwise.
One stick flat side up is Do (1), two is Gae (2), three is Geol (3), four is Yut (4), and none is Mo (5).
Yut or Mo earns another throw. When you are done throwing, split the collected results among your pieces in any order.
Land exactly on an opponent to capture and throw again. Land on your own piece to stack and move together.
A piece finishes by passing the start/finish corner. The first player to bring every piece home wins.
'vs AI' is you against 1–3 AI players; 'Pass and play' is 2–4 people sharing a device. Play with 4 pieces (default) or 2.

board.title: The board and shortcuts
items: The board has 29 spots: 20 around the square and 9 on the two diagonals crossing in the center.
A piece that stops exactly on the top-right (Mo) or top-left (Dwit-mo) corner takes the diagonal shortcut next time. Passing by keeps it on the outer path.
Stopping exactly on the center (Bang) sends the piece down the diagonal straight to the finish. Passing through the center from Mo continues toward the bottom-left corner.
Because you must pass the finish, the outer path takes 21 steps; stopping on Mo and then the center is the fastest route at 12 steps.
Arriving on Mo, Dwit-mo or the center by Backdo also counts as stopping there.

backdo.title: Backdo
items: One stick is marked. If only that stick lands flat side up, it is Backdo: move one step back. Here it is the stick with the red dot.
Going back follows the path the piece came along. Backdo from the first diagonal spot returns to Mo, which then takes the shortcut again.
Backdo from Do moves to the finish corner; from there any throw finishes the piece.
With no piece on the board, Backdo cannot be used and is discarded. Thrown together with Yut or Mo, use those first to enter a piece and then Backdo.
Backdo can capture an opponent right behind you. Turn Backdo off in settings to count the marked stick as Do.

stackCapture.title: Stacking and capturing
items: Your pieces on the same spot stack and move as one. It is faster, but a capture sends the whole stack back.
Land exactly on an opponent to capture. Captured pieces go back to waiting and you throw again.
Pieces you only pass over are not captured; only the landing spot counts.
Extra throws from Yut, Mo or a capture are thrown before you use the rest of your results.
Stacked pieces finish together, so stacking near the finish can bring several home at once.

throws.title: Throw results and odds
items: Each stick is assumed to land flat side up with probability 1/2, counting all 16 outcomes (Backdo on). The game throws with these odds.
Gae is most common at 6/16 (37.5%); Yut and Mo are 1/16 (6.25%) each. With Backdo off, Do is 4/16 (25%).
Real sticks are not exactly 50/50 because of their shape and how they are thrown, so real-life odds differ a little.

items.q: Does a piece finish if it lands exactly on the finish corner?
items.a: Here a piece must pass the finish corner. Landing exactly on it keeps it on the board, and any later throw takes it out — opponents can capture it meanwhile. Some families count landing there as finishing.

items.q: What are the odds in Yut Nori?
items.a: With 50/50 sticks: Do 4/16 (25%), Gae 6/16 (37.5%), Geol 4/16 (25%), Yut 1/16 (6.25%), Mo 1/16 (6.25%). With Backdo, 1/16 of Do becomes Backdo. Gae is the most common.

items.q: When is Backdo, and what if no piece is on the board?
items.a: Backdo happens when only the marked stick lands flat side up; the piece moves one step back along its path. With no piece on the board it is discarded. Backdo from Do moves to the finish corner.

items.q: Must a piece on Mo or the center take the shortcut?
items.a: Yes, a piece that stops on Mo, Dwit-mo or the center always takes the diagonal next. The shortcut is always shorter (from Mo: 16 steps outside vs 12 on the shortcut).

items.q: Do multiple throws have to be used in order?
items.a: No. Results collected from Yut or Mo can be used in any order on any pieces — e.g. use Do first to capture, throw again, then use the two Yuts.

items.q: What happens when a stack is captured?
items.a: Every piece in the stack goes back to waiting. Stacking is fast but risky; capturing an opponent's stack sends them all back and earns another throw.

items.q: When and with how many people is Yut Nori played?
items.a: It is a folk game families play from Seollal (Lunar New Year) to the first full moon — in 2027 Seollal is February 7, with the holiday from February 6 to 9. This game supports vs AI (you plus 1–3 AI) and 2–4 people on one device.
